meta_description: Research copilot for wealth advisors — client meeting preparation time down 60% with compliance passing 93% of outputs on first review

blocks.x: Research copilot for wealth advisors, client meeting preparation time down 60% with compliance passing 93% of outputs on first review

Identity withheld, a private banking group in the Gulf whose advisors spent their mornings assembling briefs from four research silos and their evenings defending them to compliance. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline week measured the real cost of advice: 7.2 hours of preparation per client meeting, and suitability documentation finished after the meeting, when it could no longer shape the advice.
Research arrived as PDFs with no linkage to client mandates or restrictions. Advisors paraphrased from memory, and compliance reviewed wording, not evidence.

We built the advisory copilot on retrieval: client mandate, restrictions and holdings resolved into the brief automatically, every research claim cited to its source, and the suitability record drafted alongside the brief, before the meeting. Advisors edit; the system assembles; compliance reviews evidence, not prose.

blocks.x: The pattern that travels is brief-assembly with the suitability record drafted in parallel, it has since run in two advisory businesses outside wealth. The corpus curation workflow does not; it is a mirror of each firm's research governance, and the diagnostic maps it before a single document is indexed.
Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
If this case sits close to your operation, the briefing is the right next step: 45 minutes with the practice lead who ran it, your metric against the pattern that moved here.
